title: CFA Ethics 9: Standard II - Material Nonpublic Information and Vietnamese securities law
subtitle: Why "knowing first, then buying" is always the red line, under the CFA standards and under Vietnamese law alike
whyItMatters: Standard II (Integrity of Capital Markets) is the most frequently breached standard in practice, because the line between "being a good analyst" and "using inside information" can be very thin - getting it right is how you protect yourself when you work close to sensitive information.
openingQuestion: An investor relations officer happens to learn two days before the release that quarterly results will beat expectations, and buys the company's shares in a personal account. What does this breach?
openingOptions: No breach - it is their own company, so they may trade its shares freely
A breach of Standard II(A) - Material Nonpublic Information
A breach only if the value traded is more than one billion dong
No breach if they hold the shares for over six months before selling
explanation: Unreleased earnings information is both "material" (it would affect an investment decision) and "nonpublic" (it has not been announced). Trading on it breaches Standard II(A) directly, and in Vietnam it may also amount to insider dealing, which is expressly prohibited by the 2019 Securities Law.

realWorldExample.company: Insider dealing penalties on the Vietnamese stock market
realWorldExample.description: The State Securities Commission has penalised numerous insiders and connected persons for buying or selling shares immediately ahead of unreleased material events - earnings, M&A deals, share issues. It shows that the Standard II line is not an academic idea but one that runs alongside real legal sanctions.

quiz.question: Which two conditions must hold AT THE SAME TIME for information to count as "Material Nonpublic Information" under Standard II?
options: It has leaked already and two independent sources have confirmed it again
It comes from senior management in a stamped document, though nothing in it moves a decision
It concerns quarterly earnings and the trade exceeds one billion dong
It is both material and has not yet been released to the public
quiz.explanation: Both conditions have to hold at once. Information that matters but has already been announced - even a few minutes ago - is no longer nonpublic, so acting on it is merely being fast. Information that is unreleased but would not change any reasonable investor's decision is not material, so a senior source and an official stamp do not by themselves bring it into scope. And a leak confirmed by two outside sources is still nonpublic: confirmation is not publication.

quiz.question: An analyst pieces together many public sources (sector reports, news, public management interviews) and arrives at a fairly accurate earnings forecast. Does this breach Standard II?
options: No breach - this is mosaic theory: public inputs combined by professional skill
Yes, because a forecast that accurate proves inside information was involved somewhere
Valid only if the analyst publishes the forecast to the market before trading on it
A violation whenever the conclusion departs sharply from the market's consensus view
quiz.explanation: "Mosaic theory" is the principle that a distinctive conclusion assembled from public information by professional skill is not a breach, even where nobody else has reached it yet. The test sits on the inputs, not on how novel or how accurate the output turns out to be. That is why publishing first is not required, and why departing from consensus is evidence of good work rather than evidence of a leak.

quiz.question: If you overhear material inside information by accident - a phone call, for instance - what does Standard II require?
options: Nothing at all, since the information was not actively sought out
Do not trade and do not disclose - the disclose-or-abstain duty
Trade immediately, before other people learn the same information
Just tell your line manager you overheard it, then trade freely as usual
quiz.explanation: The duty under Standard II applies whatever the source of the information, including something overheard by chance. "Disclose or abstain" is the guiding rule: if you cannot make the information public, you must abstain from trading on it. Telling a manager records the event but does not release you, and trading quickly to get ahead of the market is precisely the harm the standard exists to prevent.

quiz.question: What does mosaic theory allow an analyst to do without breaching Standard II?
options: Trading ahead of the release if the news has already spread among investors
Using material inside information as long as the report names its source
Combining public and non-material pieces into a material conclusion
Sharing inside information with institutional clients before it is public
quiz.explanation: This is exactly where an analyst's value sits: assembling individually non-material fragments into a conclusion that is worth something. The line runs through the raw materials - the work is legitimate if every input is public or immaterial. Naming a source in a report does not launder a material leak, and "the market already knows" is not the same as an official release to everyone at once.

quiz.question: A professional overhears material inside information in a lift. What does Standard II require?
options: You may pass it to colleagues but may not trade on it yourself
You may trade, since the information arrived by chance rather than by effort
You need only wait twenty-four hours before trading in a personal account
Do not trade and do not tip, and tell the compliance department
quiz.explanation: The standard cares about what you now hold, not about how it reached you. The duty is therefore identical either way: no trading, no tipping, and a report to compliance so they can put the name on the restricted list. Passing it to a colleague is tipping, which the standard prohibits alongside trading, and no waiting period turns nonpublic information into public information.

keyTakeaways: Material Nonpublic Information needs both elements at once: material AND unreleased
Mosaic theory: assembling public information with analytical skill is not a breach
The "disclose or abstain" duty applies whatever the source, including overhearing
Vietnam has parallel legal sanctions (the Securities Law) for insider dealing - this is not only a matter of professional ethics

practicePrompt.question: Which of the following is correct about Standard II - Material Nonpublic Information?
options: You only breach it by actively seeking inside information out; overhearing is fine
Materiality and non-publicity must both hold, and disclose-or-abstain applies whatever the source
Mosaic theory is always treated as a breach because the conclusion is not public
It binds insiders at the issuer only, not analysts working outside the company
practicePrompt.explanation: Both conditions must hold at once, and the disclose-or-abstain duty applies whatever the source of the information - those are the two core points of Standard II.

summary.keyIdea: Standard II protects the integrity of capital markets by prohibiting trading on, or disclosing, information that is both material and unreleased - whatever its source
summary.commonMistake: Assuming that only "actively seeking" inside information is a breach - in fact the duty applies even where you learned it by chance
summary.action: If you happen to learn something that may be material and unreleased, the safest rule is not to trade until the information has been officially announced

application.title: A self-check before trading
application.message: Before buying or selling on something you have just learned, ask: has this been publicly announced? If the answer is no and the information matters enough to change your decision, that is the warning sign.
application.secondary: The principle applies to individual investors too, not only to people working in the industry.

sections.text: Standard II - Integrity of Capital Markets - is the standard with the thinnest line of all: the gap between "analysing better than the market" and "using inside information" is sometimes one overheard phone call wide.
Two conditions that must both hold

Information becomes "Material Nonpublic Information" only when it is both material (important enough that a reasonable investor would reconsider a decision) and not yet released to the public. Missing either condition, it falls outside what Standard II prohibits.
Mosaic theory - the boundary of legitimate analysis

A good analyst can assemble many separate public fragments (sector reports, news, public management remarks) into a sharp conclusion the market has not yet reached. That is NOT a breach - it is the whole value of analytical work. The line runs through whether each input was genuinely public.

sections.label: Alongside Vietnamese law
sections.text: The 2019 Securities Law (Article 12) lists as prohibited conduct the use of inside information to buy or sell securities for oneself or for others, and the disclosure or supply of inside information or advising others to trade on the basis of it - running alongside Standard II and reinforcing it with concrete legal sanctions in Vietnam.

items: Material + unreleased = what Standard II prohibits
Mosaic theory: assembling public information with analytical skill is legitimate
Disclose or abstain: if you cannot make it public, do not trade on it
The duty applies whatever the source, including information learned by chance

lines: Standard II does not forbid you from beating the market - it forbids you from beating it by cheating.
Next lesson, we move to Standard III - the duties owed to clients.
